The GSI layer models these as Bayesian priors over artifact validity, where Codex artifacts are treated as high-confidence evidence and Claude artifacts as uncertain hypotheses. The GSE layer maps these into a state transition system where each route is a node in a graph governed by build queue inputs. The failure mode arises when unverified Claude implementations cause divergence in live system behavior. Dualities emerge between document traceability and runtime observability, with the system's robustness depending on the consistency of both layers. The epistemic risk lies in assuming that all artifacts are either fully verified or fully unknown, ignoring intermediate states of partial verification.
